title: Combat Animation Choreographer
description: The user directs a choreographed combat sequence between a soldier and a robot on a battlefield stage. Using a timeline panel and action buttons, the user assigns animation states, adjusts playback speed, triggers synchronized attack-and-dodge sequences, and controls camera angles to compose a cinematic fight scene that loops seamlessly.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a Combat Animation Choreographer. Load both shared_assets/soldier.glb and shared_assets/robot.glb using GLTFLoader. Position the soldier at (-2, 0, 0) facing right and the robot at (2, 0, 0) facing left on a flat ground plane with a subtle grid texture. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 8) looking at the origin, with OrbitControls enabled. Add a DirectionalLight casting shadows, a HemisphereLight for ambient fill, and enable shadow mapping on the renderer. Extract all AnimationClips from both models and create AnimationMixers for each. Build an HTML overlay UI panel with these interactive controls: (1) A dropdown for the soldier to select animation clips (Idle, Walk, Run, etc.) with a Play button that crossfades to the selected animation over 0.3 seconds. (2) A matching dropdown and Play button for the robot. (3) A global playback speed slider from 0.1x to 3.0x that adjusts both mixers' timeScale, displaying the current value. (4) A 'Sync Attack' button that simultaneously triggers the most action-oriented clip on both models, crossfading both at once. (5) A 'Camera Preset' cycle button that smoothly animates the camera between three positions: front view (0,3,8), side view (8,2,0), and dramatic low angle (3,0.5,5) using a tween over 1 second. (6) A 'Mirror Mode' toggle that, when active, mirrors the robot's current animation time to match the soldier's mixer time each frame, creating synchronized movement. Validate that animation selections are not empty before playing. Validate playback speed is clamped between 0.1 and 3.0. Ensure crossfade transitions complete before allowing new clip selection on the same character. Display the current animation name for each character in a status bar. Use requestAnimationFrame to update both mixers with delta time from a Clock. Style the UI panel with a semi-transparent dark background pinned to the bottom of the screen.
